title: Mastering Nullable Reference Types in C#

scenes.line1: Ever hit a null reference bug?
scenes.say: Have you ever run into a null reference bug? Let's see how C sharp helps you avoid them.

scenes.label: Nullable
scenes.sub: C# 8 lets you mark references as nullable.
scenes.say: Starting with C sharp 8, you can mark reference types as nullable. That means the compiler helps you spot potential null issues before you run your code.
Here's how you enable nullable reference types. Notice how string question mark means name can be null, and the compiler warns you if you misuse it.
Using nullable reference types catches bugs early, keeps your code safer, and shows interviewers you know modern C sharp.

scenes.question: How do you avoid null bugs in C#?
scenes.wrong: Just check for null at runtime.
scenes.right: Enable nullable reference types to catch issues at compile time.
scenes.say: In interviews, don't just say you check for null at runtime. Mention enabling nullable reference types to catch problems before your code runs.
